subject: std::bad_alloc error when estimating a value-added model (cmdstan)

messages.author: fcac2ab47b3becc5
messages.subject: std::bad_alloc error when estimating a value-added model (cmdstan)
parts:
Hello,

I have been trying to estimate a value-added model of student achievement, but I have been receiving the following error:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue: 
std::bad_alloc 
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine, 
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Once this message appears, it does not go away. It is repeated in the output file that I generate using SBATCH. 

The model explicitly allows teachers to have different effects in the year they teach students and in the (future) years when their students move to higher grades. The model also estimates the variance/covariance matrix of teacher effects for grade 1 though grade N teachers. This model was originally introduced by Mariano, McCaffrey, and Lockwood for an article in the Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics. I translated their model from WinBUGS to Stan. Currently, I am modeling four years of student achievement data. I am attaching the model code for reference. 

I am happy to provide more information. I am currently using cmdstan V. 2.5.0, and I am using a server to run cmdstan at my university. 

Given the flexibility of this model, there are many parameters that need to be estimated. Using my real data set of test scores, my output file is already 25 GB after about 2000 iterations. I think this might be the problem, but some help with confirming this error would be very helpful. 

I am attaching the stan code. I will try to create some sample simulated data later, if that is useful.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: fcac2ab47b3becc5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] std::bad_alloc error when estimating a value-added model (cmdstan)
parts:
Thanks for looking into this, Bob.

I am using a relatively new computer cluster to run my model. Here are the details of the system to which I have access :
  • Two load balanced login nodes
  • 120 general compute nodes with dual socket Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v2 @ 2.60GHz (8 core/socket); 64 GB 1866 MHz DDR3; 100 GB local SSD
  • 2 "big data" nodes with quad socket Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-4640 @ 2.40GHz (8 core/socket); 1.5 TB RAM; 13 TB local storage 
  • 5 GPU nodes with dual socket Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2640 v2 @ 2.00GHz; 256 GB RAM; 200 GB local storage
  • 2:1 oversubscribed FDR Infiniband network
  • 1 PB Lustre parallel file system for /scratch 
Here is the contents of my SBATCH program:

#!/bin/bash 
#cvamstan.sbatch, a sample slurm job  
#
#all commands that start with SBATCH contain commands that are just used by SLURM for scheduling  
#################
#set a job name  
#SBATCH --job-name=cvamV04_m_cohort2004_c1
#################  
#a file for job output, you can check job progress
#SBATCH --output=cvamV04_m_cohort2004_c1.out
#################
# a file for errors from the job
#SBATCH --error=cvamV04_m_cohort2004_c1.err
#################
#time you think you need; default is one hour
#SBATCH --time=8:00:00
#################
#quality of service; think of it as job priority
#SBATCH --qos=normal
#################
#number of nodes you are requesting
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#################
#memory per node; default is 4000 MB per CPU
#SBATCH --mem=50GB
#################
#task to run per node; each node has 16 cores, "task" is "core" really
#SBATCH --ntasks=4
#don't use --cpus-per-task on this cluster
#################

And here is the command I issue to run cmdstan:
#Chain 1
./cvamV4_4year sample num_samples=15000 num_warmup=3000 save_warmup=0 \
 random seed=5255 id=1 \
 data file=../data/RtoStanV04_m_cohort2004.dat \
 output file=../data/stanV04_m_cohort2004_c1.csv refresh=50

For now, I have been running chains separately. 

Let me know if you need more information. 

-Chris

parts:
I am attaching an R program that will assemble a data set for estimation. The R program will read in the two attached CSV files and create a data set that can be used with rstan or cmdstan. It is much smaller than my actual data set, but I have also been receiving the std::bad_alloc message using these data as well. 

I think I programmed the model correctly in stan, although the code might not be as efficient as it could be. The value-added model did work in WinBUGS, so I am hoping to have it work properly in stan. It certainly runs much faster in stan, until I get the memory error message.

By the way, here is the code I would use for rstan on my MacBookPro with 16 GB of RAM and quad-core processor:
############
# ESTIMATION
############

# (1) Translate code to C++
rt <- stanc(file="cvamV4_4year.stan", model_name = 'VAM1')
# (2) Compile code
sm <- stan_model(stanc_ret = rt, verbose = FALSE)

# Multiple chains (MacOSX)
sflist1 <- mclapply(1:4, mc.cores = 4,
                    function(i) sampling(sm, data = data1, seed = seed,
                                         chains = 1, chain_id = i, refresh = -1, iter=10000,
                                         warmup=4000, thin=1))

result1 <- sflist2stanfit(sflist1)

-Chris
